interviewQuestions.question: Why do CPUs use L1/L2/L3 instead of just one bigger, well-tuned cache?
interviewQuestions.answerMarkdown:
Access latency grows with cache size — bigger SRAM arrays have longer wire delays and need more time to search. No single size is both large enough for a modern working set and fast enough for a cycle or two.

So the hierarchy stacks several: L1 stays tiny (32-64 KB, 1-4 cycles); L2 (256 KB-2 MB) catches what L1 can't hold; L3 (tens of MB, shared) catches the rest before RAM. Each trades size for speed, keeping most accesses fast.

**Testing:** whether you see this as a physical size-vs-latency constraint, not an arbitrary choice.
interviewQuestions.subTitle: Why the hierarchy has levels
